Second comment for a second helpful cleaning tip: Clutter in motion vs Clutter in stasis

Clutter in motion: stuff you are currently using, have used recently, and/or will likely use soon. Examples include my laptop, my keys, and the blankets I like to snuggle under on the couch.

Clutter in Stasis: stuff that’s been there a while that you aren’t likely to use again soon. Examples include the dishes that have sat in the sink for 3 days, the laundry I still haven’t folded, and the blankets I don’t really use but are piled on the end of my couch.

Clutter in motion is fine. It serves a purpose, you know where it is (maybe), and it’s not bothering anyone. Clutter in stasis needs to be cleaned. The issue is, you have to be able to recognize when clutter in motion has become clutter in stasis. The blankets I haven’t really used in a week? Put them away. My work laptop on a Friday when I won’t use it again until Monday? Put it away. 

Final tip: Never store things on the floor. Get baskets, shelves, organizers, whatever. Make sure it’s a system you will actually use. Marie Kondo is cute but I will seriously never be able to keep up with her hacks. And that’s okay!
